site.title: Snapmaker Studio user guide — from install to a checked sliced job
site.description: A step-by-step, click-through guide to Snapmaker Studio v1.5.0: install, open a model, read the checks, prepare a U1 copy, hand it to Snapmaker Orca and check the sliced job.
site.disclaimer: Snapmaker Studio is an **independent open-source project — not affiliated with or endorsed by Snapmaker**. “Snapmaker” is a trademark of its respective owner.
site.footer: This guide describes **Snapmaker Studio v1.5.0**, the current stable release. Studio is advisory: it checks and prepares files, Snapmaker Orca slices, and nothing here is a promise that a print will succeed. Source, release notes and verification: [github.com/DVOpenLabs/snapmaker-studio](@repo).

welcome.title: From download to a **checked, sliced job**
welcome.lede: Snapmaker Studio checks a model and your Snapmaker U1 before a layer is sliced, prepares a safe U1 copy, hands it to Snapmaker Orca, and checks the sliced job when it comes back. This tour walks you through it, one lesson at a time.
welcome.versionLine: Guide for **Studio v1.5.0** (current stable release) · Windows and Linux · about 45 minutes for the whole tour
welcome.noJs: JavaScript is off, so every lesson is shown below on one page. Screenshots and their numbered notes are all here as plain text; only the click-through examples need JavaScript.
welcome.cardText: We begin with installing Studio, then open a model, read the checks, prepare a copy for your U1, and bring the sliced job back.

lessons.title: Install and open Snapmaker Studio
lessons.goal: Studio is installed from the official release, its download is verified, and you are looking at the Home screen.
prereq: **Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit)**, or **Linux x86_64** with a desktop. Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 are the systems Studio's Linux package has been checked on. macOS is not supported.
Nothing else to install: no Python, Node.js or Rust. There is no account to create.
steps: Open the official [Releases page](@releases) and download the Windows installer (`Snapmaker.Studio_<version>_x64-setup.exe`) or the Linux `.deb`. Download only from that page.

steps.text: Check the download. Compare its SHA256 with the value in [RELEASE_METADATA.md](@metadata); that file is the one place the current hashes are kept.
sub: If the two values differ, delete the file and download it again.

steps: **Windows:** run the installer. It is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may say **Unknown publisher**. Once the hash matches, choose **More info → Run anyway**, then start **Snapmaker Studio** from the Start menu. More detail: [Windows install guide](@windows_install).

**Linux:** run `sudo apt install ./<the .deb file name exactly as shown on the Releases page>`, then start **Snapmaker Studio** from your application menu or run `snapmaker-studio-desktop`. More detail: [Linux install guide](@linux_install).
Studio opens on **Home**. There is nothing to sign in to.
expect: A dark window with a sidebar (**Home**, **This print**, **My designs**, **Ready now**, **Printer**, **Help**) and a large **Open a model** button.
The version number at the bottom of the window reads **v1.5.0**, and the footer says **Local-only · nothing leaves your network**.

notes.text: Linux support is verified by automated installs on clean Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 systems. Other distributions and real desktops have not been recorded yet; see the [Linux install guide](@linux_install) for the current list.
Uninstalling Studio does not delete your project data. On Windows that data lives in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\SnapmakerStudio`; delete that folder yourself if you want it gone.

demo.title: Find your way around Home
demo.intro: Click the pulsing numbered circle in each step. Nothing is installed or opened; it is only a picture.

steps.instruction: Find the button that opens a model. Click circle **2**.
steps.result: **Open a model** sits at the top of the sidebar so it is always one click away.

steps.instruction: Find the switch between Simple and Advanced. Click circle **3**.
steps.result: **Simple** shows six everyday items; **Advanced** shows every tool. You can switch at any time.

steps.instruction: Find where to get help. Click circle **4**.
steps.result: **Help** has the update check and the support bundle (lesson 12).

help.if: Windows says “Windows protected your PC”.
then: That is expected for an installer that is not code-signed yet. It does not by itself mean the file is unsafe, but only continue after the SHA256 matches and you downloaded it from the official Releases page.

help.if: The hash does not match.
then: Do not run the installer. Delete it and download it again from the official Releases page.

help.if: Studio looks different from this guide.
then: This guide describes **v1.5.0**. Check the version at the bottom of the Studio window. Newer releases may move things; the [release notes](@releases) say what changed.

lessons.title: Open your first model
lessons.goal: A model is open in Studio and you know what Studio learned from it.
prereq: An `.stl` or `.3mf` file. The repository's [`examples` folder](@examples) has two small ones: `sample_cube.stl` and `demo_offplate_foreign.3mf`. This lesson uses the cube.

explain.title: STL or 3MF? What Studio can learn from each

items.text: An STL describes a surface and nothing else: no colours, no print settings. Studio measures it and says: “This STL does not include creator slicer settings. Studio will use a U1 starter profile unless you choose another Orca profile.”

A 3MF can hold the shape **and** colours, separate parts and often the creator's print settings. Studio can compare those with your U1, point out settings that came from another printer, and keep the creator's settings when it prepares a copy.

steps: Press **Open a model** (top of the sidebar, or the large button on Home), or drag the file onto the Studio window.
Choose `sample_cube.stl`.
Studio opens the **Workspace** and reads the file on your computer; nothing is uploaded.
Read the status line under the file name, the verdict banner (**Can prepare a U1 copy**) and the **What's in this design** card.
expect: The status line reads **Checked — here's what we found. Press Prepare U1 copy when you're set.**

**What's in this design** says *a plain model (STL)*, **20 × 20 × 20 mm**, 0 colors, 0 parts and a rough filament cost. The cost uses a default price per kilo that you can change in **Settings → Filament price**.
Nothing has been prepared yet, and your file has not been touched.

notes.text: Studio shows a rough filament cost from a default price per kilo. It is an estimate for orientation, not a quote.

demo.title: Open the example cube
demo.intro: Follow the circles through the first minute with `sample_cube.stl`.

steps.instruction: Start on Home and click circle **1**, **Open a model**.
steps.result: A file picker opens on your computer. You would choose `sample_cube.stl`.

steps.instruction: Studio now shows the Workspace. Click circle **2** to read the verdict.
steps.result: **Can prepare a U1 copy**: the file can be prepared. It is advice about preparing, not a promise about the print.

steps.instruction: Click circle **5** to see what Studio measured.
steps.result: A plain STL model, 20 × 20 × 20 mm, no colours, no parts, and a rough filament cost.

help.if: Nothing seems to happen after choosing a file, or the page says “Couldn’t read that file”.
then: The file may be damaged or may not really be an STL or 3MF. Download it again.

Open **Compatibility** (lesson 4). For a damaged 3MF it says **Studio could not open this file as a 3MF project.** The Workspace can look normal for such a file, so check Compatibility if something seems off.

help.if: My own model shows different numbers.
then: That is expected: the numbers describe your file. Only the example cube is exactly 20 mm.

lessons.title: Understand “This print”
lessons.goal: You can tell where you are in the job, what Studio knows and what to do next.
prereq: A model open in Studio. This lesson uses `demo_offplate_foreign.3mf` from the [examples](@examples).
steps: Open **This print** in the sidebar (it is called **This Print** in Advanced view).
Read the page title, **This print — your file name**. Everything on the page is about that one job.
Stage **1. Before slicing**: **Object placement**, **Before you slice** and **Colours and toolheads**. These compare the project with the printer Studio can see.
Stage **2. Prepared**: until you prepare a copy it says **Nothing prepared yet.** After you prepare one, this stage shows what changed (lesson 6).
Stage **3. After slicing**: where the sliced job comes back (lesson 9).

Switch the sidebar between **Simple** and **Advanced** with the **View** toggle at the bottom, or under **Settings → Mode**. Simple lists Home, This print, My designs, Ready now, Printer and Help, with the rest under **More tools**; Advanced lists everything.
expect: Three numbered stages, top to bottom, in the order a job actually happens.
With no printer connected, checks that need a printer say **Studio can’t tell** instead of guessing. That is correct, not an error.

notes.text: “Studio can’t tell” means Studio has no way to read that fact from your printer. It does not mean your printer cannot do it. Those are the items to check yourself.

demo.title: Follow one job through This print
demo.intro: Click each pulsing circle to step through the three stages.

steps.result: **Before slicing** compares the project with the printer Studio can see right now.
With no printer connected, each answer is marked **Studio can’t tell**, and each says what to do.
**Prepared** stays empty until you prepare a copy. Preparing never touches your original.
**After slicing** is where Snapmaker Orca's result comes back for checking. Studio does not slice.

help.if: The page says “Open a model to start”.
then: No project is open. Press **Open a model**, or open one from **My designs**.

help.if: Cards show “Checking…” for a while.
then: Studio first tries to reach a printer. When none answers, the cards switch to **Printer not found** and **Studio can’t tell**. This can take a little while.

help.if: I cannot find a tool the guide mentions.
then: You are probably in Simple view. Open **More tools**, or switch to **Advanced** with the **View** toggle.

lessons.title: Read the checks
lessons.goal: You can tell a problem that needs attention from a heads-up, and both from something Studio cannot know.

items.text: Something in the project is likely to cause trouble in Orca. For a downloaded project it often means settings from another printer; the model itself may be fine.
Worth knowing. Often a thing Studio cannot verify, such as object-to-object spacing.
Studio cannot read this from your printer. Check it yourself; the card says how.
Studio checked and found nothing wrong. It is still advice, not a guarantee.

steps: Open **Compatibility**: in Advanced view it is in the sidebar, in Simple view it is under **More tools**, or press **Open the full checks** on **This print**.
Read **Object placement** first. The example says **1 object is outside the U1's printable area.** and names the object and the distance.
Scroll to the summary, for example **Found 5 invalid-value issue(s) and 2 warning(s).** Each card has a label, an explanation and a **Do this:** line.
Read each **Do this:** line. Open **Technical detail** only if you are curious; you never need it to follow this guide.
Notice the banner on the Workspace (**Needs a fix first** or **Can prepare a U1 copy**). It summarises the checks; it is not a verdict on the print.
expect: A list of cards, each with a label, plain-language text and a next step.

For the example: a placement finding with a **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)** button, several **NEEDS ATTENTION** findings about settings from another printer, and **HEADS UP** findings such as **Profile may not be a Snapmaker U1 profile**.

notes.text: The checks are read-only. Studio never edits your file while diagnosing it.
Studio does not yet check spacing between objects in a multi-part layout. It says so, and tells you to use **Arrange** and watch for collision warnings in Snapmaker Orca.

demo.title: Read a finding
demo.intro: Click through one placement problem and two findings.

steps.result: One object is outside the printable area, and the card names the object and the distance.
This file likely carries settings from another printer. The text says the model may be fine; the project settings are the problem.
A concrete next step, such as importing the model into a clean U1 project, or preparing a U1 copy.
Anything that needs a printer is marked **Studio can’t tell**. You check those yourself.

help.if: The findings say “Invalid value for …”. Is my model broken?
then: Usually not. The text says the model may be fine and the project settings are for another printer. Preparing a U1 copy is designed for exactly this.

help.if: My findings differ from the example.
then: They describe your own file, so they will differ. The labels mean the same thing.

lessons.next: Fix the placement and prepare a U1 copy.

lessons.title: Fix placement and prepare a U1 copy
lessons.goal: The off-plate object is back on the plate in a new copy, and a U1 copy has been prepared from it.
prereq: `demo_offplate_foreign.3mf` open. In the example, the second object hangs 55 mm past the right edge of the plate.
steps: On **Compatibility**, **This print** or the Workspace, find **Object placement**: *Object 2 · 20 × 20 × 20 mm — Hangs 55.0 mm past the right edge.*
Press **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)**.

The card turns green: **The object sits inside the U1's printable area.** with the line *1 object(s) moved onto the U1 plate in a new copy — demo_offplate_foreign_placed_U1.3mf. Your original file was not changed.*
The copy is saved next to your original. **Copy file location** copies where it is.
That copy has its objects on the plate but still carries the original's settings. Press **Open a model** and choose `demo_offplate_foreign_placed_U1.3mf`.
On the Workspace, leave **Preserve creator settings** (marked *Recommended*) selected and press **Prepare U1 copy**.
expect: A banner reading **U1 copy created — review setup before slicing**, saying your original file is not modified.

New files beside your original: `demo_offplate_foreign_placed_U1.3mf` (the moved copy) and `demo_offplate_foreign_placed_U1_SnapmakerU1.3mf` (the prepared copy). You may also see a file ending in `.orig.3mf`: an untouched snapshot Studio keeps next to a prepared copy.
If you open the prepared copy, **Object placement** now says the object sits inside the printable area.

items.text: Keeps the print looking the way the creator intended, and changes only the minimum needed for Snapmaker Orca to open it. The right choice for a downloaded model.

items.h: Use Studio's U1 starter settings instead
items.text: Replaces the creator's print settings with Studio's U1 defaults. Speed, temperature, retraction, supports and cooling will change. Useful when the file was made for a very different printer.
Review the settings yourself before preparing.

notes.text: Moving and preparing both write **new** files. Your original is never modified, and the moved copy changes only where the objects sit: layout, rotation, scale and height stay as the creator set them.

**Move onto the plate** and **Prepare U1 copy** are two separate actions. Moving writes a repositioned copy; to get a U1 copy that is also on the plate, prepare the moved copy as in steps 5 and 6. Preparing the original on its own does not move anything, and the result still says print-setup risks remain.

demo.title: Fix placement, then prepare
demo.intro: A five-step example of the whole fix. Nothing is written; it only moves between pictures.

steps.result: One object hangs 55.0 mm past the right edge.

steps.instruction: Click circle **3**, **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)**.
steps.result: Studio writes a new file with every object shifted onto the plate.

steps.instruction: Click circle **1** to read the result.
steps.result: The object was moved in a new copy, and your original file was not changed. Open that copy next.

steps.instruction: With the moved copy open, click circle **3**, **Prepare U1 copy**.
steps.result: Studio prepares a U1 copy using **Preserve creator settings**.

steps.instruction: Click circle **1** to confirm the result.
steps.result: **U1 copy created**, and your original is untouched. Next, review what changed.

help.if: There is no **Move onto the plate** button.
then: Either every object is already on the plate, or one move cannot fix the layout. The card then says so and tells you to open the project in Snapmaker Orca and use **Arrange**.

help.if: The prepared copy still shows warnings.
then: Studio prepares the file for the U1; it does not fix every setting. Read the remaining findings and the **Your fix plan** list, which marks each step **Do this in Studio** or **Do this in Orca**.

help.if: I do not know which file is which.
then: The names say it: `…_placed_U1` was moved, `…_SnapmakerU1` was prepared, and your original keeps its own name.

lessons.title: Review what changed
lessons.goal: You can say what Studio kept, what it changed, what it could not carry over and what it could not check.
steps: After preparing, scroll to **What survived preparing this copy**. The example says **14 kept · 2 changed**; your counts will differ.
Expand **What Studio changed (n)**, then **What stayed the same (n)**.
Scroll to **Changes Studio made**. Each numbered action shows how many changes it made, that the structure was validated, and the file it produced. **Before and after** shows exact values.
Look further down for **Kept from the original file** (for example *533 creator settings kept*), **Adjusted for U1 project compatibility**, and **Optional recommendations (not applied)**.
If you want to go back, **Return to the original** points Studio at your untouched file. The copy stays on disk.
expect: A before-and-after comparison. Settings Studio could not carry over appear under **What Studio could not carry over**, and anything it could not identify is listed as unverified rather than assumed to be fine.
Optional recommendations stay **not applied** unless you choose them.

notes.text: **Return to the original** never writes to your original. Everything Studio makes is saved as a new file.
“Unverified” is a real answer. When Studio cannot identify something in both files it says so instead of calling it fine.

demo.title: Review a prepared copy
demo.intro: Click through what a prepared copy tells you.

steps.result: A comparison of everything Studio can identify in the original and the copy, with how many settings were kept and how many Studio changed.
Expand it to see each change. Nothing is changed silently.
A numbered list of actions, each with the file it produced and a **Before and after** view.
Studio points back at your untouched file; the copy stays on disk.

help.if: My numbers differ from the guide.
then: They describe your file. The structure of the report is the same.

help.if: I want to undo a preparation.
then: Your original was never changed, so there is nothing to undo. Delete the copy if you do not want it.

lessons.title: Plan colours and materials
lessons.goal: You know whether your colours fit the U1's four toolheads and, if you track spools, which spool and Orca preset each colour maps to.
prereq: A multi-colour project open. This lesson uses `demo_u1_showcase.3mf` from the [examples](@examples).
steps: Open **Colors & Materials** (Advanced sidebar, or **More tools**).
Read **Colours and toolheads**. The example says **6 colours, 4 toolheads — possible without repainting.**
Read the groups: **Not proven separable — reserve a toolhead each**, **Appear only higher up — could be a planned swap**, and **Studio can’t tell how these are used**.
For a painted project, a box says how many filament colours the painting uses. Expand **What Studio read from the painting** for the measurements.

To change one plate's colour, use **Plate Color Remap** at the top of the same page: **Open a 3MF project**, choose the plate (the buttons are labelled **Plate 1**, **Plate 2** and so on), choose the colour to replace and the colour to use, press **Preview changes**, then **Create remapped copy — original stays unchanged**.
Optional, if you use a spool tracker: open **Compatibility** and read **Project materials** (below).
expect: A plain sentence comparing your colours with the four toolheads, then the reasons.
A closing line: **Load the colours in the order the project lists them.**

explain.title: Assigning a colour is not loading filament

items.text: Studio reads which colour each part of the project uses and plans toolheads. It can write a chosen colour into a **new** copy.
Putting the right filament in the right toolhead is a physical job only you do. Studio never loads, swaps or changes spools, and it never writes to your spool tracker.

branches.title: Project Materials (v1.5)
branches.when: You track spools in Spoolman, SpoolEase or Bambuddy and want each colour tied to a real spool and an installed Orca preset.
steps: Set a provider once in **Settings → Materials provider** (optional; without one you can still choose presets).
On **Compatibility**, find **Project materials**. For each slot Studio lists up to three spools with reasons. **No spool is selected for you.**
Select the spool that is physically in your hand, then press **Use this preset** (the suggestion) or **Choose an installed preset**, or **Keep project's filament**.
Press **Review & prepare**, read the review, then **Prepare with these choices**.
Tick **Remember this mapping** if you want it reused. It is saved only after the copy is written, and checked again every time.
branches.see: Orca's own installed presets can be checked against the U1 and your nozzle and are shown as **Proven**. Presets you made yourself are shown as **Confirmed by you** and **Manual check in Orca required**: Studio cannot confirm Orca applies their temperature, flow and cooling, so check the filament in Orca before slicing. If two slots share one preset but disagree about vendor or type, Studio stops with **Prepare stopped** and explains why.

notes.text: The number four comes from the U1's published four toolheads. Studio says it did not read it from a printer.
Project Materials does not create custom Orca presets, choose a spool for you, write to your spool provider, or promise that Orca applies a preset you made yourself.

demo.title: Plan colours, then choose a spool
demo.intro: Click through the colour check and the first Project Materials choices.

steps.result: 6 colours on 4 toolheads: possible without repainting, because some colours only appear higher up and can be planned swaps.

steps.instruction: Click circle **3** to see what a toolhead is.
steps.result: A toolhead melts one filament. The U1 has four, so it can print four colours at once.
Studio says why it suggested the spool. You pick the one that is physically in your hand.

steps.instruction: Click circle **3**, the Orca preset area.
steps.result: Nothing is chosen yet. **Use this preset**, **Choose an installed preset** and **Keep project's filament** are your options.

steps.instruction: After choosing, click circle **1**, the review.
steps.result: A plain list of what will be written. Press **Prepare with these choices** only when it looks right.

help.if: Colours are listed under “Studio can’t tell how these are used”.
then: The project does not say which object, painted region or colour change uses that slot. Load the colours in the order the project lists them, and check in Orca.

help.if: There are no spool suggestions.
then: No provider is set up, or none matches the material. You can still choose an installed preset for a slot, or keep the project's filament.

help.if: **Prepare stopped** appears.
then: Two slots share one preset but the project declares different vendors or types for them. Choose a different preset for one slot, or remove the declaration in the source project. Studio does not edit it for you.

lessons.next: Open the prepared copy in Snapmaker Orca.

lessons.title: Open the prepared copy in Snapmaker Orca
lessons.goal: Your prepared copy is open in Snapmaker Orca, you have reviewed it there, sliced it and exported the G-code.
prereq: [Snapmaker Orca](@orca) installed. Studio never slices; Snapmaker Orca does.
steps: On the prepared result, press **Open in Snapmaker Orca**. If Studio cannot find Orca the button reads **Install Snapmaker Orca** instead; install Orca, or press **Copy path** and open the file from Orca yourself.

In Orca, check before slicing: the printer is **Snapmaker U1**, the filaments and colours match what you will load, the objects are on the plate (use Orca's **Arrange** if you are unsure), and supports are set the way you want. Studio's **Your fix plan** marks these as **Do this in Orca**.
Slice in Orca (its **Slice plate** button).
Export the G-code from Orca and note where it is saved. Orca's menu wording can differ between versions, so use Orca's own export command.
Keep the exported `.gcode`. If you want your Orca settings kept too, also save the project from Orca.
expect: Orca opens your prepared copy. Studio stays as it was: it does not control Orca and does not slice.
After slicing you have an exported `.gcode` file ready for lesson 9.

notes.text: The handoff is one-way. Studio opens the file in Orca and does nothing else with it.
Studio's copy is a starting point. Always review it in Orca before slicing; the report from lesson 6 lists what Studio changed.

demo.title: From prepared copy to Orca
demo.intro: Three steps in Studio. The slicing itself happens in Snapmaker Orca, which this guide does not simulate.

steps.instruction: Start from the prepared result. Click circle **1**.
steps.result: Your U1 copy is ready, and your original is untouched.
In the real app this opens the prepared file in Snapmaker Orca. This example never launches anything.

steps.instruction: Click circle **4** to read what happens next.
steps.result: Slice in Snapmaker Orca and export the G-code. Then return to Studio to check the sliced job.

help.if: The button says **Install Snapmaker Orca**.
then: Studio did not find Orca. Install it from the [releases page](@orca), then prepare again or use **Copy path** and open the file from Orca.

help.if: Studio says “Couldn’t launch Snapmaker Orca — open the file from Orca instead.”
then: Open the prepared file from inside Orca. Use **Copy path** to find it.

help.if: Studio says “Couldn’t find the prepared file — try preparing it again.”
then: The copy was moved or deleted. Prepare it again.

help.if: Orca shows a “Customized Preset” notice.
then: That can happen when the creator's tuned settings are kept. Review the settings in Orca before slicing.

lessons.next: Bring the sliced job back to Studio.

lessons.title: Bring the sliced job back
lessons.goal: Studio has read your exported G-code and told you what it can confirm and what it cannot.
prereq: An exported `.gcode` file from Snapmaker Orca (lesson 8). The pictures here use a small example job written for this guide.
steps: Open **After Slicing**: Advanced sidebar, **More tools**, or stage 3 of **This print**.
Optional: type the folder where Orca saves exports and press **Watch this folder**. Studio looks there only while this page is open.
Otherwise drag the `.gcode` onto the window or paste its full path into **Open the G-code your slicer produced**, then press **Check this job**.
Read **Ready to send?** and the findings under it. Each states what Studio found, what to do, and where it came from.
Read **What the printer will actually do**: *sliced by*, *for*, *prints from*, *layers*, *estimated time*, *filament* and *file*.
Scroll to **What to load** for what each slot needs, and **What happens during this print** (**Read the whole job**) for the job in order.
expect: An answer such as **Nothing blocks this job, but 1 thing(s) are worth settling before you send it.**
Facts read from the file itself, such as **Snapmaker Orca 2.3.4**, **Snapmaker U1**, **12 at 0.2 mm** and the slicer's own time estimate.
With no printer connected, anything that depends on the machine reads **Studio can’t check this**, followed by what to do.

notes.text: Studio reads the file, not the world. With no printer connected it cannot tell which tools are present, whether the slots are loaded, whether the bed matches or which nozzle is fitted, and it says so.
Studio reads and never changes your G-code, and it never sends anything on its own.

demo.title: Check a sliced job
demo.intro: An example with a made-up job. Studio is not connected to anything.

steps.result: You drag in or paste the path of the `.gcode` file Orca exported.
Studio reads the job and compares it with the project and, when connected, the printer.
The overall answer and what is worth settling first. It is never a promise that the print will succeed.
Unknown stays unknown: with no printer connected, machine-dependent facts are listed rather than guessed.
Sliced by, for, prints from, layers, time and filament, all read from the file.

help.if: Nothing appears in the watched folder.
then: Check the folder is the one Orca exports to, and that this page is open. Studio only looks while the page is open. You can always paste the file's path instead.

help.if: Studio says it cannot tie the job to my project.
then: Nothing in either file identifies the model, so Studio cannot tell whether this is the slice of the project you checked. Make sure you picked the right file.

help.if: Many items say “Studio can’t check this”.
then: That is what honest looks like with no printer connected. Connect the printer (lesson 10) or check those items yourself.

lessons.next: Connect your printer and check readiness.

lessons.title: Connect your printer and check readiness
lessons.goal: Studio can read your U1's live state, you know what stays unknown, and you know which actions ask you to confirm.
prereq: Your U1 is on, and on the same network as this computer.
On the U1's touchscreen, Advanced Mode is on under **Settings → Maintenance**. Studio's own message says the printer's network interface only opens once it is turned on.
steps: Open **Printer** (Simple view) or **Printer Hub** (Advanced).
Under **Connect to your U1**, type the printer's network name (the field starts with `U1.local`) or its IP address and press **Connect**, or press **Auto-detect my U1**.
To keep the address, set it under **Settings → Printer → Network name or IP**.
Read what Printer Hub reports. Anything the printer does not tell Studio says so, for example **Nozzle sizes: not reported**, instead of being guessed.
If the printer does not report its nozzles, you can tell Studio what is fitted under **Settings → Nozzles**. Those entries are labelled **Confirmed by you**.
Open **Ready now** and press **Check my library**. Studio sorts your library into **Needs preparation**, **Needs attention**, **Can’t determine**, **One change away** and **Ready now**.
expect: When your printer answers, Printer Hub shows its live status and the controls become available. When it does not, **Controls are off until the printer is connected and reachable.**
**Ready now** says it is advisory only: it uses your library, your printer's reported state and the filament inventory you configured, and changes nothing on your printer.

items.text: Run as soon as you press them. They are reversible.
Asks first: *Cancel this print?* A cancelled print cannot be resumed.

items.h: Upload sliced gcode, then Start this print
items.text: You choose the file to upload. **Start this print** then asks: *Start printing this file?* Studio does not check the bed for you.
Asks first. It halts motion and heaters and may need a firmware restart before printing again.

notes.text: Monitoring is read-only. Studio never starts a print by itself; anything that moves the printer or sends a file happens only when you press the button and confirm.
Studio does not guess. If the printer does not report a fact, it stays **not reported** until you confirm it, and a fact you confirmed is labelled **Confirmed by you**.
This guide has no screenshot of a connected printer: no printer was contacted while it was written. The pictures show Printer Hub exactly as it looks before a printer answers.

demo.title: Connect, in pictures
demo.intro: This example cannot connect to anything. It only shows where you would click.

steps.result: You would type your U1's network name or IP address here.
Studio would ask your printer, on your own network, for its state. This example does not.
Until a printer answers, controls stay off. When one does, Pause, Resume, Cancel print, Upload sliced gcode and Emergency stop appear, and the risky ones ask you to confirm.

help.if: Printer Hub says “Printer not found”.
then: Studio asked the address and nothing answered. Check the printer is on and on this network, and that the address is the one it shows. On a U1, turn on Advanced Mode under **Settings → Maintenance** on the touchscreen.

help.if: Auto-detect finds nothing.
then: Type the printer's name or IP address instead and press **Connect**.

help.if: The controls are greyed out.
then: They are off until the printer is connected and reachable. That is deliberate.

help.if: **Nozzle size** says Studio can’t tell.
then: The printer did not report it. Check the nozzle on the printer, and, if you like, record it under **Settings → Nozzles**.

lessons.title: Explore additional tools
lessons.goal: You know which optional tool to reach for, and what each one will and will not do.
steps: Pick the tool that matches your question from the cards below. None of them is needed for the main tour.
Most tools work on the model that is currently open. Open one first with **Open a model**.
In Simple view, find them under **More tools**.
expect: Each tool reads or prepares a copy and never changes your original file.

branches.title: Cost & Pricing Doctor
branches.when: What does this print cost, and what could I sell it for?
steps: Open **Cost & Pricing Doctor**.
Read **Cost Doctor**, **Pricing Doctor** and **Profit Doctor**.
Press **Show details & assumptions**.
Set your own spool price under **Settings → Filament price**.
branches.see: All figures come from your own assumptions. They are rough estimates, not financial advice.

branches.title: Scale Doctor
branches.when: I want to resize a model.
steps: Open **Scale Doctor**.
Enter a **Scale %** and press **Preview**.
For an STL, **Prepare scaled copy** writes a new file.
For a 3MF, preview here and resize in Snapmaker Orca; Studio will not write a scaled 3MF it cannot stand behind.
branches.see: Uniform scaling only. Your original is never changed.

branches.title: Print Quality and First Layer
steps: Open **Print Quality** and use its **Print Quality** or **First Layer** tab.
Pick the symptom that looks like your print.
Read the likely causes and safe first checks.
branches.see: Advisory only. It never changes your settings or G-code.

branches.title: Projects (My designs)
branches.when: I want to find a project I already checked.
steps: Open **My designs** (Simple) or **Projects** (Advanced).
Use **All**, **Profile compatible** or **Needs prep** to filter.
Open a design again, or open its **History**.
branches.see: Studio lists projects you have checked or prepared.

branches.title: Batch Prepare
branches.when: I have many files to prepare.
steps: Open **Batch Prepare**.
Press **Add files** and choose your `.stl` and `.3mf` files.
Press **Prepare**. Studio prepares a U1 copy of each.
Review each copy in Snapmaker Orca.
branches.see: Each file is prepared separately and nothing is modified in place.

branches.title: Find Models
branches.when: I want to browse model sites from inside Studio.
steps: Open **Find Models** and pick a site, such as Printables or MakerWorld.
Browse and download with the site's normal download button.
Studio adds supported downloads to your Library.
Check it in **Ready now**.
branches.see: Sign in on the site itself; Studio never sees your password. **Clear site data** signs you out of every site.

branches.title: Materials providers
branches.when: I track my spools in Spoolman, SpoolEase or Bambuddy.
steps: Open **Settings → Materials provider**.
Choose **Spoolman**, **Bambuddy** or **SpoolEase** and enter its address.
Use **Your spool notes** for anything the printer and provider do not report.
branches.see: Studio only reads from a provider; it never changes it. The printer always wins about what is loaded.

help.if: A tool does not show in the sidebar.
then: Switch to **Advanced** view, or open **More tools** in Simple view.

help.if: A tool says it needs an open model.
then: Open one with **Open a model** first.

lessons.title: When something goes wrong
lessons.goal: You can find your problem by its symptom, update Studio safely and send a useful report.
steps: Find your version: it is shown at the bottom of the Studio window (for this guide, **v1.5.0**).

To look for a newer version, open **Help → Check for a newer version** and press **Check GitHub now**. Studio never updates itself or downloads anything; it only tells you a version number and a link.
To update, download the new installer from the official Releases page, verify its hash, and run it over your existing install. Your data is kept. There is no in-app auto-update.

To report a problem, open **Help → Reporting something Studio got wrong**, press **Show me what it contains** and read it, then **Save it to a file**. Your username, home folder, file paths, machine name and printer address are replaced first, and Studio never sends the bundle anywhere.
Open a report on the [Studio issues page](@issues), attach the saved bundle, and say what you did, what you saw and what you expected.
expect: The update check reports a version number and a link, nothing more.
A bundle you have read before it is written to disk.

notes.text: The update check makes one request to GitHub asking which release is newest, and sends nothing about you or your files. The automatic check is off until you turn it on, and runs at most once a day.
If your result differs from this guide, check three things first: the version, which file you have open, and whether a printer is connected. Many answers change with those.

help.if: A file will not open.
then: Download it again. For a 3MF, **Compatibility** says **Studio could not open this file as a 3MF project.** if it is damaged. If the Workspace looks normal but nothing else works, trust Compatibility.

help.if: Preparing fails or stops.
then: Studio shows the reason on the page. For **Prepare stopped** in Project Materials, read the explanation: it names the slots and the conflict. Otherwise open the original in Snapmaker Orca to see whether it opens there, then report it with a support bundle.

help.if: Studio cannot find Snapmaker Orca.
then: The button reads **Install Snapmaker Orca**. Install Orca, or use **Copy path** and open the prepared file from Orca.

help.if: The printer is unreachable.
then: Check it is on and on this network, that the address is right, and that Advanced Mode is on under **Settings → Maintenance** on the touchscreen. Then press **Connect** again.

help.if: Nozzle or material information says Studio can’t tell.
then: That is expected when the printer or provider does not report it. Check the printer, and optionally record nozzles under **Settings → Nozzles** and spools under **Your spool notes**.

help.if: The result looks different from this guide.
then: Check the version, the file and whether a printer is connected. If it still differs, send a support bundle with your report.

help.if: Something looks wrong with a print after slicing.
then: Use **Print Quality** (lesson 11) to pick the symptom for likely causes and safe first checks.

lessons.next: That is the whole tour. Keep [RELEASE_METADATA.md](@metadata) and the [verification record](@trust) for the current hashes and test results, and use **Start again** to walk it once more.
